headline: The US Treasury Secretary says Washington will propose an emergency AI notification channel with China.
score_reason: A concrete US-China AI safety proposal from a cabinet member, but a proposal only and reported by one outlet.
importance_line: A formal way for the two AI superpowers to warn each other when an AI system goes wrong would lower the risk of an incident escalating, but China has not agreed and the idea exists so far only in an interview.
summary: Axios reports, as relayed by The News International, that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the US will propose a notification process with China for use when something goes wrong with an AI system, adding that he assumes Beijing will agree after he and Vice Premier He Lifeng discussed AI safety before Xi Jinping's state visit last month. Bessent said Chinese officials "didn't realize how powerful their open source models are" and argued the US should spend more effort protecting critical systems from AI threats than making models stronger; no agreement has been announced.
notes: Axios page blocked by Cloudflare; text read from The News International (thenews.com.pk), which credits Axios.
